article.description: — Andrew Meadow scored a career-high 28 points, Fred Payne had 23, and Oregon rolled past Maryland 88-73 on Friday in the seventh-place game at the Players Era 16.

article.story: LAS VEGAS, Nev. -- — Andrew Meadow scored a career-high 28 points, Fred Payne had 23, and Oregon rolled past Maryland 88-73 on Friday in the seventh-place game at the Players Era 16. Meadow, a transfer from Boise State, and Payne, who transferred from Boston College, combined to make 22 of 30 shots while the Ducks hit 57% as a team. The Ducks had only six turnovers compared to Maryland's 15. Oregon had a 21-7 advantage in turning turnovers into points. Mike McNair Jr. and Pharrel Payne each scored 15 points, Baba Oladotun 12 off the bench, and Kaden House 11 for Maryland (3-5). Jasper Johnson scored 10 for Oregon (4-3). Maryland managed one field goal in the first 7 1/2 minutes of the second half and Oregon's 15-0 run contributed to a 58-40 lead. The Terrapins made only six field goals through the first 17 minutes of the half while Oregon maintained a big lead — a dunk by Meadow giving the Ducks an 84-61 lead. Meadow scored 10 points in a 12-0 run that gave the Ducks an 18-10 lead eight minutes into the game. The Ducks' lead was 30-29 before Meadow hit a 3-pointer and Seven Spurlock followed with a dunk to restore a five-point cushion. Meadow had 15 points in the half and Oregon led 40-35 at the break. Up next Oregon: The Ducks open Big Ten play at UCLA on Tuesday. Maryland: The Terps host American on Wednesday. -------- Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here.
